I realise that most of these are in the header file, but as per another comment, I'm not sure that the header file is needed.  Are there any out-of-tree users of the header file?

This contains a lot of duplication of what was just merged in !2983 (with changes pending in !4427). Can this duplication please be removed and instead use the `wscbor_*` API? The function signatures are almost identical to this old `bp_cbor_*` API.

How does this CBOR, wscbor_* and the older CBOR dissector (packet-cbor.c) relate? Don't they all decode the same CBOR format? For me it looks like wscbor_* should use functions from `packet-cbor.c` to properly show the decoded values.

The CBOR _dissector_ in `packet-cbor.c` is for displaying raw (schema-less) decoded CBOR. That is fine when needed, but when a protocol uses CBOR within a higher-level schema we don't want to see "array of int and bstr", we want to see for example "a time in seconds and a checksum".
The `wscbor` API is not itself a dissector, it is for dissectors to safely and robustly extract item-level data (e.g. int64 values) from an encoded octet stream.
Thank you for this clarification. So ideally we should now use `wscbor` API in `packet-cbor.c`?

Not really; the CBOR dissector in `packet-cbor.c` doesn't really care about the high-level that `wscbor` provides the API for, it is visualization closer to the encoding. Because CBOR is so syntactically simple, the duplication/overlap between the two is really on the level of a couple of functions that aren't even in the public API for `wscbor` right now.

With `packet-cbor.c` you _see_ the tags and the distinction between different encoding forms (integer bit lengths). With the `wscbor` API that is intentionally hidden under "get the int64 value, however encoded".
This is really not a safe way to read (variable-length) CBOR data. The `wscbor` API allows reading CBOR items in a safe, robust way.
The [source](https://github.com/BrianSipos/dtn-wireshark) that this was copied from is **not** GPL, it's LGPL. This copy, if accepted, must stay LGPL.

I really recommend to keep the original separation of layers from the [repository](https://github.com/BrianSipos/dtn-wireshark) this was copied from; instead of pulling everything together in one source file. This makes extending with new block types much more difficult later on. The BPv7 API was put in a header for a reason.

@lindnerp can we coordinate on getting an up-to-date BPv7+BPSec integrated in a robust way?

I would prefer to pull out BPv6 and TCPCLv3 from the `packet-dtn.h/c` into their own dissectors, and implement the version-switching logic within the `packet-dtn.c`.
@BrianSipos yes, that can be done.

I have proposed a merge !4497 based on a more recent upstream `dtn-wireshark` repo.

This other merge _does not_ (yet) include the BPSec default security context registration though. Do you have an example pcap handy to validate that context's parameters/results?

@lindnerp The other MR now has dissectors for default security context parameters and results, and a couple of single-bundle test captures are added. Would you be willing to verify that other MR branch looks acceptable and to have that MR supersede this one?
mentioned in merge request !4497
None of these enumerations are even used by a dissector. Your implementation doesn't actually register BPSec default context parameters or results. Did those get left out?
